newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU energy consumption up 3.6 percent in 1996.
newsitem.headline: EU energy consumption up 3.6 percent in 1996.

text.p: European Union total gross inland energy consumption rose 3.6 percent last year to reach 1,360.4 million tonnes of oil equivalent, Eurostat said on Thursday.
The 15-nation bloc's energy dependency rate -- net imports as a proportion of gross consumption -- remained at 48.2 percent, it said. Two thirds of this was petroleum.
Twelve member states were above this figure and net-exporting Britain and low import dependency in the Netherlands and Denmark kept the average down.
Gross inland consumption rose sharply in Nordic EU members Denmark, Sweden and Finland -- up by 13.8, 12.6 and 10.3 percent respectively.
It rose by 5.7 percent in Britain, by 4.4 percent in France and by 3.6 percent in Germany. But consumption fell by 0.7 percent in Italy and by 3.8 percent in Spain.
The highest average energy consumption per capita was in Luxembourg while Portugal recorded the lowest consumption level.
Eurostat also said total consumption of hard coal fell by 3.8 percent, oil consumption rose by 2.4 percent while natural gas soared 11.6 percent, due mainly to increased use in power generation.
Nuclear energy accounted for the largest share of EU production.
